content: Pravastatin is a medication prescribed to help lower cholesterol and other fatty substances in the blood. It is used in combination with lifestyle changes, such as following a low-fat, low-cholesterol diet, engaging in regular physical activity, and losing weight if necessary. Pravastatin belongs to a class of drugs called HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, commonly known as statins. It works by reducing the production of cholesterol in the body. High levels of cholesterol and fats can accumulate along the walls of blood vessels, leading to a condition called atherosclerosis, which restricts blood flow and oxygen supply to vital organs like the heart and brain. By lowering cholesterol levels, pravastatin can reduce the risk of developing heart disease, angina (chest pain), strokes, and heart attacks. Pravastatin is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. It is important to take the medication at the same time each day and follow the instructions provided by your doctor or pharmacist. Do not take more or less of the medication than prescribed. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it, but no more frequently than once every four weeks. Even if you feel well, continue taking pravastatin as directed. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Before starting pravastatin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pravastatin or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and non-prescription drugs, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as cimetidine, cyclosporine, ketoconazole, other cholesterol-lowering drugs (e.g., fenofibrate, gemfibrozil, niacin), and spironolactone, may interact with pravastatin. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. If you are taking cholestyramine or colestipol, take them four hours before or one hour after pravastatin. If you use antacids, take them one hour before pravastatin. Inform your doctor if you have liver disease, as pravastatin is contraindicated in such cases. Additionally, disclose if you consume large amounts of alcohol, have a history of liver or kidney disease, or are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking pravastatin, stop the medication immediately and contact your doctor, as it may harm the fetus. Do not breastfeed while taking pravastatin. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking pravastatin. Ask your doctor about the safe consumption of alcohol while on this medication, as alcohol can increase the risk of serious side effects. While taking pravastatin, adhere to a low-cholesterol, low-fat diet. This includes foods like fat-free milk, cottage cheese, fish (not canned in oil), vegetables, poultry, egg whites, and polyunsaturated oils (e.g., corn, safflower, canola, soybean). Avoid high-fat foods such as fatty meats, liver, egg yolks, whole milk, cream, butter, shortening, lard, pastries, cakes, cookies, peanut butter, chocolate, olives, potato chips, coconut, cheese (except cottage cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, and fried foods. If you miss a dose of pravastatin, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Pravastatin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include heartburn and headache. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, require immediate medical attention. These include muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; lack of energy; fever; yellowing of the skin or eyes; upper right abdominal pain; nausea; extreme fatigue; unusual bleeding or bruising; loss of appetite; flu-like symptoms; rash; hives; itching; difficulty breathing or swallowing; swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; and hoarseness. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store pravastatin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments while taking pravastatin. Your doctor will order tests to monitor your response to the medication. Inform laboratory personnel that you are taking pravastatin before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Pravastatin is sold under the brand names Pravachol® and Pravigard® PAC.
